reviews.text:
Excellent, but learn to use it. Read instructions here.. I like this because it's nice and simple, free, and does everything I need. It's also very accurate, IF you know how to use it.

I downloaded this app for my 4th generation iPod touch a few months ago. I was totally frustrated with it, because it was terrible at recording my steps. I removed it, disgusted.

Then I thought about it. It uses the iPod's (or iPhone's) three-axis accelerometer, a trick device. It should work fine, and if it doesn't, it's probably not the app's fault. For any pedometer, to work, it has to "feel" at least a small bump, each time you step. Like coins jiggling in your pocket. Anything that might prevent coins jingling in your pocket might prevent a pedometer from working accurately. If you've got other stuff in your pocket, which might cushion the bump a little, or maybe very loose fitting clothes, an elastic waistband, etc., that can interfere with proper operation.

The great thing about this product that it works in any orientation. It will pick up bumps whether it is right side up, sideways or cockeyed. By comparison, the kind you buy at the sporting goods store only work in one axis, up and down. You have to clip them on just right and if they get knocked askew, they don't work.

This app works just fine if you just drop your iPhone or iPod in your pocket. Whether it works well in your purse depends on a number of factors, mentioned previously.

Whether it works well held in your hand depends on how you hold it. If you hold it in your hand like you're carrying a full cup of coffee, you smooth out the bumps and it won't record your steps accurately.

Now that I've figured out how to use this thing, I've walked to the corner many times, fast or slow, in different clothes, different shoes. It always records 600 steps, give or take two or three. I'm pretty sure this is accurate. When I enter the distance to the corner and the length of my stride, it comes out exactly right.

reviews.text:
When it works, it. I have the paid version, and while I'm aware I only spent ninety-nine cents on it, I'd still like to see it be a little more reliable. The thing is that my neighbor and I can walk 6 days a week, and for 5 it might be fine, but then one day it will tell me I walked 11 minutes (we walk about an hour). We've had fun watching our average MPH increase, checking how far we've gone, how long we've walked, and then randomly, it won't work at all. I can carry it in the pocket of a fleece vest and it works fine, but in the pocket of a hoodie it stops and starts. I put it in an Armpocket the other day, and it recorded half the walk. I feel like I always need a backup plan if I want to actually use my walk as "exercise". Since I'm using Lose It!, I want to know if I walked for 35 minutes, or 55.

I have to say that when it stays on for the entire walk, it's great. I just don't understand why it does or doesn't always do that.

Not so good. I have had nothing but bad luck with this app! I really wanted it to work but each time I tried there was a problem. 
1) I pressed start and started walking - locked my phone so I didn't press any buttons. Once I got home I unlocked my phone to realise the app pauses when the phone is locked. That's ok - I found out how to lock it so it keeps working. 
2) The next day I tried again. Off I went only to find that once you get to 3000 steps you have to buy the full version. That's fair enough. It said it if I bought the full version it would transfer my current steps over so I could proceed. It did not. Never mind, I thought. There is always tomorrow. 
3) Day three and I set out again to try this app. It got to 2990 steps and it froze. 
My experience hasn't been so great and I don't think I'll bother using it again.
